input.quote: Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Sections 13.1–13.3 already meet the preferred position for the Services and paid-up software licences (Affiliates and contractors covered, perpetual and irrevocable paid-up licence, transfer to Affiliate/successor, revocation only for uncured material breach). Section 14.2, however, gives Customer only a revocable, non-transferable Deliverable licence limited to the Order Form term — revocable at Vendor's discretion, excluding Affiliates and contractors, and with no successor transfer. That conflicts with the rule and with the bargain in 13.2–13.3, so 14.2 is redlined to align (Vendor ownership of Deliverables left intact).

proposal.summary: Align the Deliverable licence in 14.2 with the perpetual, irrevocable, transferable licence terms in 13.2–13.3, and extend it to Affiliates and contractors.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have aligned the Deliverable licence with the paid-up licence terms already agreed in Sections 13.2 and 13.3, so it runs to our Affiliates and contractors, is perpetual and transferable to a successor, and is revocable only for uncured material breach. Our playbook does not permit a licence that Vendor can revoke at will or that expires with the Order Form term, since we continue to rely on Deliverables after that term ends.

ops.oldText: Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
ops.newText: Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf receive a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, reproduce, display, modify, and create derivative works from each Deliverable for their business purposes, transferable to an Affiliate or successor as provided in Section 13.3 and revocable or suspendable only on the terms set out in Section 13.3.
